slokas.meaning: When will that day come when I wander through the forests of Vrindavan upon the vast, sandy banks of the pure Yamuna River? There, I long to see Lord Govinda strolling alongside His brother Haladhara (Balarama) and His dear friend Sudama. Crying out intensely, "O Krishna! O my Master! O All-pervading One who captivates everyone with the sweet music of Your flute, please be merciful to me!", I wish to pass my days so absorbed in devotion that years pass by in the blink of an eye.

When will I walk along the shores of the Yamuna River (Kalindi), which are completely adorned and sanctified by the footprints of Sri Hari? While walking, I want to constantly remember Gopinatha (the Lord of the Gopis), visualizing His lotus-like eyes and gently smiling face. Crying out, "O Embodiment of absolute bliss, whose face is like a blooming lotus, O protector and lover of Your devotees, be pleased with me!", I wish to spend my days in this divine ecstasy.

sanskrit: अये राधे किं वा हरसि रसिके कञ्चुकयुगं
english: aye rādhe kiṁ vā harasi rasike kañcuka-yugaṁ
slokas.meaning: Sometimes, I long to see Him playing joyfully in the neighborhoods of Vraj with the cowherd boys—that radiant, extraordinary young boy of the cowherds who appeared from some mysterious divine realm. I long to witness His sweet, loving pastimes as He playfully teases, "O Radha! O beautiful queen of divine rasas, why have You hidden My garment?" Witnessing these playful pastimes and crying out, "O Lord, bless me!", I wish to spend all my days.

Sometimes, I wish to see Him standing in the midst of the Gopis, dancing with exquisite grace like a master actor, while the Gopis gaze at Him with surprised, laughing, and deeply affectionate eyes. This is the very same Sri Hari whose lotus feet are continuously praised by all the rulers of the heavens (Indra and the Gods). Calling out to that supreme dancer, "Be pleased with me!", I want my days to pass like a fleeting moment.

Sometimes, I long to see the Lord of the Yadus (Krishna) resting under the cool, soothing shade of a tree, waving one of His beautiful hands like the moving border of a garment, inviting devotees into peaceful meditation. Calling out, "O generous Lord of the devotees, with a face like a lotus, O beloved son of Nanda Baba, show me Your grace!", I wish to spend my days fully immersed in Your thought.

Sometimes, I wish to visualize Him perched high up on the branches of the Kadamba tree on the banks of the Yamuna River, smiling knowingly and playfully having taken away the clothes of the meditating Gopis to teach them absolute surrender. Praying to Him, "O Lord who brings joy to Indra, O Lifter of the Govardhan Hill, be pleased with me!", I wish to spend my life crying out for Your vision.

sanskrit: वदन्तं पार्थेति नृपसुत सखे बन्धुरिति च ।
english: vadantaṁ pārtheti nṛpa-suta sakhe bandhuriti ca |
slokas.meaning: Sometimes, I want to see Him in the forests acting as the dearest friend and guide to Prince Arjuna (Vijaya), affectionately calling out to him, "O Partha! O prince, my friend, my brother!" I long to see Sri Hari wandering, resting, and holding the divine flute close to His lips. Calling out to this compassionate friend of Arjuna, "Please be merciful to me!", I desire to pass my days.

When, at last, will I truly behold this flawless, Supreme Divine Being with lotus-like eyes? O Lord Vishnu! O supreme Master of Yoga! O enchanting player of the flute who relishes the spiritual essence of love! It is only fitting for You, who are an ocean of boundless mercy, to shower grace upon a poor, helpless soul like me. Constantly weeping and crying out, "O Lord, have mercy and show Yourself!", I wish to spend every single day of my life.

sanskrit: नासाग्रे नवमौक्तिकं करतले वेणुं करे कंकणम् ।
सर्वांगे हरिचंदनं सुललितं कंठे च मुक्तावलिं
english: nāsāgre navamauktikaṃ karatale veṇuṃ kare kaṃkaṇam .
sarvāṃge haricaṃdanaṃ sulalitaṃ kaṃṭhe ca muktāvaliṃ
slokas.meaning: With the fragrant kasturi-mark on the forehead, the precious Kaustubha gem on the chest, the lovely pearl-jewel at the nose tip, the flute in the palm and the kankan (bangle) encircling the hand, the scented sandalwood paste all over the body, the pearl-necklace around the beautiful neck, surrounded by milk-maids - may victory be yours, O crown gem of Gopalas.

"I worship Lord Govinda, whose complexion is as radiant as a fully blossomed blue lotus, and whose face shines like the moon. He loves his peacock-feather crown, bears the sacred Śrīvatsa mark, and wears the magnificent Kaustubha gem along with beautiful yellow garments. His divine form is lovingly worshipped by the lotus-like eyes of the gopīs, and he is always surrounded by cows and cowherds. I bow to that beautiful Lord, who is absorbed in playing melodious tunes on his flute, and whose limbs are adorned with celestial ornaments."

sanskrit: बिभ्रद् वास: कनककपिशं वैजयन्तीं च मालाम् ।
english: bibhrad vāsaḥ kanaka-kapiśaṁ vaijayantīṁ ca mālām
slokas.meaning: Wearing a peacock-feather ornament upon His head, blue karṇikāra flowers on His ears, a yellow garment as brilliant as gold, and the Vaijayantī garland, Lord Kṛṣṇa exhibited His transcendental form as the greatest of dancers as He entered the forest of Vṛndāvana, beautifying it with the marks of His footprints. He filled the holes of His flute with the nectar of His lips, and the cowherd boys sang His glories.

"In the beginning, He was born from the womb of Mother Devaki, and He grew up in the home of the gopis. He destroyed the life of the treacherous demoness Putana and lifted the Govardhana hill. He executed the slaying of Kamsa, caused the destruction of the wicked Kauravas, and protected the sons of Queen Kunti. This is the essence of the sacred Bhagavata Purana, which chronicles the immortal, nectar-like pastimes of Lord Shri Krishna."
